correctness.rationale: For fixed unital A=K[t]/(t^3), require associative bilinear star and mixed associativity of m0+s*star; do not require shared unit. The mixed identity is an integer linear system of rank 18 in 27 structure constants even in characteristics 2,3,5, yielding the stated unique nine-parameter commutative table. The 27 star-associators force six equations: bf=be=0,bd+cf=bg+cd=bj+ce=b(h-a)+cj=0. If b!=0, star is multiplication by a+bt+ct²; if b=0,c!=0, force d=e=f=j=0 and leave a,c,g,h; if b=c=0 the whole associativity ideal set-theoretically reduces to 3 minors of M=[[f,d],[j,h-a],[d-e,g-j]]. Hence the reduced variety is exactly A³, A⁴, and A¹ × determinantal rank≤1 Mat_{3×2}, dimensions 3,4,5. All components are geometrically irreducible over any field, and inclusion–exclusion over intersections A²,A³,A¹,triple A¹ yields #=q^5+2q^4-2q². The motive and zeta follow by same stratification. Independent exhaustive direct nine-parameter associator evaluation for q=2,3 gives 56,387, respectively. This does not establish the unreduced scheme structure.

originality.rationale: The best-matching published classification by Abdelwahab–Kaygorodov–Makhlouf concerns 2D compatible associative/pre-Lie pairs and not the 3D fixed unital K[t]/t³ fiber. Chtioui–Das–Mabrouk establish general mixed associativity and cohomology but no irreducible-component census. Abdurasulov–Adashev–Toshtemirova (2026) use stronger matching/interchangeable identities on a *nonunital* nilpotent truncated algebra, so their special families do not imply this full unital fiber. Odesskii–Sokolov emphasize semisimple first products. Checked Resultary related 3D associative classifications lacked the same fixed-product geometry. Thus component sizes and q-counts survive the actual prior implications, subject to a possible unindexed deformation-variety computation.

value.rationale: This is a complete component/point-count/motivic classification of a natural three-dimensional local associative algebra's compatibility fiber over every field, including positive characteristic. The components' differing dimensions expose actual deformation geometry beyond a tiny numerical example or a repackaging of general cohomology. The labeled q-polynomial and zeta are natural exact invariants; no claim to classify all three-dimensional isomorphism types.

limitations: Labeled products on the fixed vector space and first multiplication, not isomorphism classes.
No classification of arbitrary three-dimensional compatible pairs or nonreduced scheme structure.
